title: Array Nesting
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, which is a permutation of numbers from 0 to n-1, construct a set s[k] starting with nums[k] and continuing with nums[nums[k]], nums[nums[nums[k]]], and so on, until a duplicate is encountered.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, which is a permutation of numbers from 0 to n-1, construct a set s[k] starting with nums[k] and continuing with nums[nums[k]], nums[nums[nums[k]]], and so on, until a duplicate is encountered. Return the maximum size of any such set s[k].
constraints: nums is a permutation of 0 through n-1.
hints: A permutation decomposes into disjoint cycles.
Once a cycle has been counted, no later start inside it can improve the answer.
Follow each unvisited start until it reaches seen values; track the length.
Marking values globally makes the total traversal linear because each array index is visited at most once.
editorial: Marking values globally makes the total traversal linear because each array index is visited at most once.

tests.explanation: Starting at 0 visits 5, 6, 2, 0, so the largest set has four values.
The self-loop contains one distinct value.
